implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.py defines BOARD_SIZE = 15 and Board.__init__(self, size=15) creates a 15×15 grid.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players (black and white) alternate turns
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py creates Player objects for BLACK and WHITE, tracks current_color, and toggles it after each successful move. ConsoleUI and GomokuGUI both display the current player.
Board.place_stone checks is_valid_move (bounds and EMPTY) before assigning the color. Game.play_turn calls this method.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Win detection for five in a row (horizontal, vertical, diagonal)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win iterates over four directions and counts consecutive stones; returns True when count >= 5. Game.play_turn uses this to set winner_color and winning_line.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full returns True when no EMPTY cells remain; Game.play_turn marks game_over with winner_color = None in that case.
console_ui.py implements ConsoleUI with render_board, parse_move, get_move, and a game loop that calls Game.play_turn.
gui.py defines GomokuGUI that draws the board, handles mouse clicks, updates status, and highlights the winning line.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Entry point that prefers GUI and falls back to console
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py defines gui_available() and main() which selects GomokuGUI if possible, otherwise ConsoleUI.

judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable Gomoku implementation: a 15×15 board, alternating black/white players, move validation, win/draw detection, and both console and Tkinter GUIs. All core requirements are satisfied and the code appears ready to execute.
